note.explanation: To find a molecular formula, first find the mass of the empirical formula. Divide the compound’s molar mass by that mass to get n. Multiply every subscript in the empirical formula by n.
examples: Empirical formula CH₂O, molar mass 180: empirical formula mass = 30, n = 180/30 = 6, so molecular formula = C₆H₁₂O₆.
Empirical formula CH, molar mass 78: empirical formula mass = 13, n = 78/13 = 6, so molecular formula = C₆H₆.
note.simple: The empirical formula is the smallest atom-count ratio. The molecular formula tells the actual number of each type of atom in one molecule.
note.checkQuestion: The empirical formula of a compound is NO₂ and its molar mass is 92 g mol⁻¹. What is its molecular formula?
note.title: Finding a molecular formula
steps: Calculate n = molar mass / empirical formula mass.
Multiply every subscript in the empirical formula by n.
note.answer: For empirical formula NO₂, the empirical formula mass is 46. Since 92/46 = 2, multiply both subscripts by 2 to get N₂O₄.

mcqs.stem: A compound has empirical formula CO₂ and molar mass 176 g mol⁻¹. What is n? (C = 12, O = 16)
rationales: This is not correct because the empirical formula mass is 44, and 176/44 is not 2.
This is not correct because 176 divided by the empirical formula mass 44 is not 3.
Correct: empirical formula mass = 12 + 2(16) = 44, so n = 176/44 = 4.
This is not correct because 44 × 6 = 264, not 176.

written.text: Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: An empirical formula gives only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, so different compounds can have the same empirical formula. A molecular formula gives the actual numbers of atoms in a molecule. For example, glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and ethanoic acid (C₂H₄O₂) both have empirical formula CH₂O. Some different compounds, called isomers, can also have the same molecular formula but different structures.

written.text: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: Sand has a giant structure, not separate SiO₂ molecules. Its formula SiO₂ represents the simplest whole-number ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms in the structure: 1:2.

explain.title: Empirical formula
explain.body: Your textbook explains: “To calculate the empirical formula of a compound, you need to determine the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in the compound.” It is the simplest ratio, not necessarily the actual number of atoms in a molecule.

explain.title: Molecular formula
explain.body: Your textbook states: “Molecular formula of a compound can be found out if we know its empirical formula.” The molecular formula gives the actual number of each type of atom in a molecule.

explain.title: Calculate the multiplier
explain.body: Your textbook gives the relationship: “Molecular formula = n (Empirical Formula)” and “Where n = Molar Mass / Empirical Formula mass”. Calculate n, then multiply every subscript by it. If n is one, the molecular and empirical formulas are the same.

mistakes: Using the molar mass as n without dividing by the empirical formula mass.
Forgetting to calculate the empirical formula mass using the correct atomic masses.
Multiplying only one subscript instead of every subscript in the empirical formula.
Leaving the final result in bracket form instead of writing the molecular formula in its simplest notation.
Treating an empirical formula as if it always gives the actual atom counts in a molecule.
